8:36.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ, καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ· τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι;
8:36.targetText: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”

groups.note: This καί, which in the Greek joins said to came, is rendered by the and BSB places before came.
κωλύει ("prevents") is rendered to prevent within BSB's question frame what is there.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame; the Greek has only Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ ("Look, water").
English supplies the frame what is there; the Greek asks τί κωλύει ("what prevents").

8:38.sourceText: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα, καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ, ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος, καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν.
8:38.targetText: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The τε of τε … καί is rendered only by the following and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending of ἐβάπτισεν.

8:39.sourceText: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος, Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον, καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος, ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων.
8:39.targetText: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.

groups.note: οὐκ … οὐκέτι ("not … any longer") is rendered no more.
BSB renders γάρ ("for") here as but.

8:40.sourceText: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον, καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάριαν.
8:40.targetText: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ ἐλθεῖν ("the coming") is rendered came.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
